line: You crashed into the planet you just left. That takes real talent.
Earth is behind you. You were supposed to go away from it.
Congratulations, you've invented the most expensive boomerang.
Gravity is not a suggestion, pilot. The big round things are hard to miss.
You were trying to fly past it, not into it. Did you think the planet would move?
Impact confirmed. Another probe, another crater.
My species has a word for that maneuver. It translates to 'lawn dart.'
You hit the Moon. It's the closest thing in the sky, and you still missed the gap.
It's a rock that's been there for four billion years. It didn't move.
Mars is red because of rust and embarrassment. You've added to the second one.
Venus is the hottest planet. Your probe's new job is as a very small meteor.
Jupiter is the largest planet in your system, and you still found a way to miss the part where you don't hit it.
You flew into Saturn's rings. They're famous. That's why people look at them from far away.
You made it all the way to Neptune just to crash. That's commitment to failure.
A rock. You hit a rock. Space is mostly empty, and you found the one thing in it.
The debris field was clearly marked. By me. You didn't listen.
Your probe is now confetti. Well done.
You left the map. Nobody told you to leave the map.
Your probe is now drifting forever. It'll make a lovely tourist attraction.
That was too much power and too little aim. Mostly the second one.
That's three in a row. I'm starting to think it's deliberate.
I've seen toddlers with better trajectory control, and they were throwing spaghetti.
Please let me fly. I promise to be gentle about your feelings afterward.
On my planet, we'd hold a funeral for the probes you've wasted.
And she's off. Try not to hit anything.
Launching. I've already prepared my disappointment.
Fingers crossed. I have six, and they're all crossed.
Not bad, human. That was only somewhat embarrassing.
You did it. I'd say I'm proud, but that would be a lie, and also against my programming.
Three stars. All beacons. I take back about a third of the insults.
A perfect run. Statistically, even a broken clock gets a perfect run once.
Using autopilot? Fine. Watch a professional.
Plotting the route. Take notes, you'll need them.
Autopilot engaged. Please take your hands off everything.
Mission one. Use the Moon as a slingshot. It's the easiest one, so don't ruin it.
Mission two. Mars, with asteroids in the way. This is where the amateurs fall off.
Mission three. Venus is heavy and pulls hard. Use it, don't fight it.
Mission four. The asteroid belt. Thread the gap. Try to be precise instead of lucky.
Mission five. Jupiter and Ganymede, a double assist. Choose a path and commit.
Mission six. Saturn's rings and two moons tugging at you. Think of it as a hard group project.
Mission seven. Uranus and Neptune. They're far, cold, and rude.
Final mission. Three giants, a moving moon, and a crowded debris field. Good luck. You've earned my respect, a little.
You did it. The edge of the solar system. I'm contacting my species. They won't believe it either.
Are you planning to launch, or are we just admiring the view?
Take your time. I only have a few more million years.
